new.s: What was the earlier name of Muhammad bin Tughlaq?
new.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq was called Juna Khan (also Ulugh Khan) before he became Sultan; Ghazi Malik was his father Ghiyasuddin.
new.angle: U0109 PYQ yc2ad770f183 MBT identity (real name Juna Khan)

new.s: Firoz Shah Tughlaq set up an employment bureau to help which of the following?
new.x: Firoz Shah Tughlaq opened an employment exchange to find work for the unemployed; slaves were looked after by the Diwan-i-Bandagan.

new.s: Which Sultan of Delhi is known for laying out about 1,200 fruit gardens near Delhi?
new.x: Firoz Shah Tughlaq planted about 1,200 orchards near Delhi and restored 30 gardens of Alauddin.

new.s: Which historian remarked on the death of Muhammad bin Tughlaq that 'the king was freed from his people and they from their king'?
new.x: The remark is by Badauni; Barani called MBT a 'mixture of opposites'.
new.angle: U0109 #15 Historians' remarks on the death of Sultans (Badauni)

new.s: Under which pen name did Sikandar Lodi write Persian poetry?
new.x: Sikandar Lodi wrote Persian verse as Gulrukhi; Tuti-i-Hind was Amir Khusrau and Sikandar-i-Sani was Alauddin Khalji.

new.s: Which tax did Sikandar Lodi abolish?
new.x: Sikandar Lodi abolished the tax on grains and several trade restrictions; he imposed jizya rather than abolishing it.

new.s: Which city was founded by Sikandar Lodi in 1504?
new.x: Sikandar Lodi founded Agra in 1504 and shifted his capital there; Jaunpur and Hisar were Firoz's towns and Siri was Alauddin's.
new.angle: U0110 #1 / PYQ yd4fac91ddc2 Sikandar Lodi -> city founded

new.s: In which year did Timur invade India and sack Delhi?
new.x: Timur crossed the Indus and sacked Delhi in December 1398, in the reign of Nasiruddin Mahmud Shah Tughlaq.

new.s: Who among the following invaded India and sacked Delhi during the reign of Nasiruddin Mahmud Shah Tughlaq?
new.x: Timur (Tamerlane) sacked Delhi in 1398 when the last Tughlaq, Nasiruddin Mahmud Shah, was on the throne.
new.angle: U0110 PYQ y55e1f0151aa identity of the 14th-century conqueror (Timur)

new.s: Which of the following was a result of the First Battle of Panipat?
o: Babur captured Delhi, Agra and the Lodi treasure
Sher Shah founded the Sur dynasty
new.x: After killing Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat in 1526, Babur took Delhi, Agra and the Lodi treasure.
new.angle: U0110 #7 / PYQ y4e8ac165c5e Panipat consequences (Delhi and Agra captured)

new.s: Why is the Battle of Khanwa regarded as more decisive than the First Battle of Panipat?
o: Artillery was used in India for the first time in it
Ibrahim Lodi was killed in it
Rana Sanga was a stronger enemy and its result set up Mughal supremacy in North India
new.x: At Khanwa (1527) Babur broke Rajput power under Rana Sanga, a stronger foe than Ibrahim Lodi, and set Mughal rule on firm ground.
new.angle: U0110 PYQ yb0fbf46ad33 Khanwa as real beginning of the Mughal empire

new.s:
What is the correct chronological order of the following dynasties of the Delhi Sultanate?
1. Tughlaq
2. Mamluk
3. Lodi
4. Khalji
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
new.x: The order was Mamluk (1206) - Khalji (1290) - Tughlaq (1320) - Sayyid (1414) - Lodi (1451).

new.s: Through which general did Alauddin Khalji begin the conquest of South India?
new.x: Alauddin Khalji's southern campaigns were led by Malik Kafur; the conquest was completed under Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
new.angle: U0111 PYQ yc998bd5adda conquest of South India -> Sultan/general

new.s: Who captured the Kakatiya ruler Prataparudra II in 1323 and annexed the Kakatiya kingdom?
o: Ulugh Khan (the future Muhammad bin Tughlaq)
new.x: In 1323 Ulugh Khan, the future Muhammad bin Tughlaq, took Warangal, captured Prataparudra II and annexed the Kakatiya kingdom.
new.angle: U0111 PYQ yc998bd5adda southern conquest completed by MBT (AP angle)

new.s: Who was the master of Qutbuddin Aibak, the first Sultan of Delhi?
new.x: Aibak was a slave and general of Muhammad Ghori, after whose death he ruled at Lahore.
new.angle: U0111 #4 first Sultan and his master

new.s: What was the holder of an iqta called in the Delhi Sultanate?
new.x: The iqta holder was the muqti (wali for a province); the amil collected revenue in a pargana and the patwari was the village accountant.
